desc: Derive correct combinatorial decomposition: f(p) = S(p) - sum over hole points q<=p of c(q)*C(p-q), with c(q) = 1 + [qx=L]*S(L-1,qy) + [qy=D]*S(qx,D-1) (the "+1" accounts for paths starting inside the hole — key fix found during verification).

Derive closed-form region sums: answer = sum over blocks of S(p) minus sum over hole of c(q)*(S(W-qx,H-qy) - S(R-qx,U-qy)); the "1" part of c collapses to O(1) G-function rectangle sums; edge parts are O(U-D) and O(R-L) loops.
Hand-verify formula against sample 1 (W=4,H=3,L=1,R=2,D=2,U=3) -> 192, matches brute-force DP.
Implement final Python solution (factorials to W+H+5, S/G helpers with negative-arg guards, O(boundary) edge loops, modular positivity) reading stdin and writing answer.

Cross-check implementation correctness (sample 1 verified exactly against brute-force DP; decomposition proven; edge cases L=0/D=0 handled by zero-weight guards) and audit loop performance (table-lookup-only binomials, single pow for inverse factorial, factorial bound W+H+4 sufficient, ~2*10^6 loop iterations).
